guide.summary: Pandas, city museums and the Wuhou Shrine, with Taikoo Li cafés and tea houses, hotel restaurants and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
highlights: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
guide.tip: Reserve the Panda Base online with real-name ID up to 14 days ahead, and plan around Mondays: the Chengdu Museum, plus Giant Panda Villa No. 6 and the Panda Art Museum at the Panda Base, close on Mondays except public holidays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Chengdu Museum, plus Giant Panda Villa No. 6 and the Panda Art Museum at the Panda Base, close on Mondays except public holidays. Wuhou Shrine Museum's homepage gives no weekly closing day.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Panda Base tickets are reserved online, valid only on the chosen date, and checked against the original ID you booked with; an adult ticket is CNY 55. Wuhou Shrine Museum charges ¥50 and says it has never authorised anyone to sell its tickets online.

toolkit.label: Queues and timing
toolkit.copy: The Chengdu Museum limits visitors to 20,000 a day and asks you to avoid 10:00–12:00 and 14:00–16:00. At the Panda Base, afternoon ticket holders are asked not to arrive early.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: The Panda Base bans drones, pets, scooters, bicycles and camera flashes. The Chengdu Museum bars pets, smelly or sticky food and coloured liquids.

guide.dek: Book the Panda Base before anything else, keep museums off your Monday plans, and anchor meals around Taikoo Li and Niccolo Chengdu at IFS.
intro: Start at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, at 1375 Panda Avenue in Chenghua District. Entry needs a real-name online reservation, made up to 14 days ahead, and you must show the original ID you booked with; an adult ticket is CNY 55, while visitors aged 60 and over and children aged 6 and under (or under 1.3 m) are exempt from reservation. From November to February, morning entry runs 8:00 to 12:00 and afternoon entry 12:00 to 16:30, with clearance from 17:30; from March to October entry opens at 7:30. Drones, pets and camera flashes are not allowed.

In the centre, the Chengdu Museum stands at No. 1 Xiaohe Street on the west side of Tianfu Square. It is closed on Mondays except public holidays, opens 9:00 to 17:00 from Tuesday to Thursday and on Sunday, and stays open until 20:30 on Friday and Saturday for its Weekend Children's Museum. The museum limits visits to 20,000 people a day and asks you to avoid the 10:00–12:00 and 14:00–16:00 peaks. Its permanent galleries include Chinese shadow puppetry and puppet exhibitions on the fifth floor.

Wuhou Shrine Museum, at 231 Wuhouci Street, lists hours of 09:00 to 18:00 with ticket sales ending at 17:00, and notes that summer extended hours and free cultural events can change them. A full ticket is ¥50 and a half-price ticket ¥25. The museum states that it has never authorised any organisation or individual to sell its tickets or guided-tour tickets online, so book through its own channels. Its 2026 bulletins cover Mid-Autumn and National Day themed events, and its current notices concern upkeep in the Jinli cultural street it manages.

For eating and drinking, Taikoo Li Chengdu, beside the ancient Daci Temple and the Chunxi Road shopping area, lists cafés, tea houses and restaurants in its directory, from %Arabica and Starbucks Reserve Bar Mixato to Jade Garden and Tasty Congee & Noodle Wantun Shop. Upper House Chengdu, at No. 81 Bitieshi Street, runs the Michelin-starred vegetarian Mi Xun Teahouse, The Temple Café with breakfast from 7am, Tivano, and the speakeasy Jing, open daily 5pm to 1am. At Niccolo Chengdu in Chengdu IFS Tower 3, The Bar on the 3rd floor has a live band from Tuesday to Sunday.
summaryCards: Reserve the Panda Base with real-name ID and pair it with the Chengdu Museum on Tianfu Square, remembering that the museum, plus Giant Panda Villa No. 6 and the Panda Art Museum at the Panda Base, close on Mondays except public holidays.
Start with breakfast at The Temple Café from 7am or Niccolo Kitchen from 6:30am, then take tea at CreaTea or coffee at %Arabica in Taikoo Li.

Reserve the Panda Base up to 14 days ahead with the ID you will carry, request Mi Xun Teahouse, Tivano and Jing tables through Upper House Chengdu's booking emails, and buy Wuhou Shrine tickets only through the museum's own channels.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Taikoo Li shops and restaurants were confirmed only through the mall operator's online directory, whose store pages give unit numbers and hours but little or no description and carry no dates of their own, so their hours are attributed to that directory; Niccolo Chengdu's dining pages show posted hours but no dated 2026 content except The Tea Lounge's 2026 menu. Upper House Chengdu (formerly The Temple House) books its restaurants by email. Wuhou Shrine Museum publishes no weekly closing day. The Sichuan Museum site returned only its title, the Du Fu Thatched Cottage site refused connection, the Chengdu IFS site timed out, and Shangri-La Chengdu blocked automated reading (HTTP 403). People's Park, Kuanzhai Alley, Wenshu Monastery and several other sights have no official website we could find. The Jinsha Site Museum is closed until 30 April 2027 according to its own site.
